study.question: Does the supplied linear history boundary account for the observed utility of order, or does relative circular event order retain predictive value after a content-defined origin and orientation treatment?
study.hypothesis: Observed: supplied AUC0.6685268680 versus lexical0.6659442302 and hash_a/hash_b0.6658821613/0.6660822710 under matched capacity; all are one frozen training seed. Full reversal0.6683840769 is close to supplied, whereas block canonicalization0.6660661993, local duplicate0.6658825133 and scrambled basis0.6666401406 lose quality. Coordinate transport recovers0.6684626464, showing optimization/coordinates matter. These trajectories do not distinguish a useful linear endpoint from relative event arrangements. Hypothesis: relative order contributes beyond event content even when the original start is removed, so minimum cyclic rotation beats lexical order at fixed learned capacity. Removing direction as well may retain that advantage given the reversal result. This is a local diagnostic hypothesis, not a novelty claim or established mechanism. It uses supplied index order only, with no timestamp or recency-in-time interpretation.

nearest_work.difference: All learned operators and source gates are inherited. Add exact cyclic/dihedral canonicalization before embedding and compression; no new learned representation or attention architecture.

Existing hash/lexical canonicalization removes all order. New cyclic rotation quotients only rotations; dihedral treatment additionally quotients reversal while preserving circular adjacency. Reuse complete-tuple gather boundary, replacing hash construction with exact prefix ranks.

Archived primary text lines56-100 describes target-dependent local activation and weighted sum. This candidate retains the inherited adapted scorer, multi-task compressed summaries and product context branch and changes event layout; it is not an original-DIN reproduction.

Pinned benchmark forward175-200 flattens item sequence before unified tokenization. No flatten/token-mixing architecture is adopted; this study isolates history symmetries inside the existing compressed joint model. Original-method equivalence unverified.

Pinned benchmark forward113-145 pools sequence then mixes field/task tokens. No such replacement is implemented; only pre-embedding input layout changes. No original-method effectiveness or priority claim.

study.proposed_difference: Compute an exact rank of each complete valid event tuple, compact the valid sequence only for index construction, and rank all forward/reversed circular rotations together by seven prefix-doubling steps (128 symbols cover maximum100). Select the lexicographically minimum forward rotation for canonical_ring, minimum across both orientations for canonical_dihedral, fully sorted tuples for lexical_bridge, or identity for supplied_bridge. Repeated minima are resolved by the entire circular sequence, not original-index ties; periodic ties are indistinguishable tuples. Map selected events back into the original valid destinations, keeping invalid positions and current targets untouched. All four modules execute all index construction and common gathers; learned capacity/RNG unchanged. Cyclic treatment retains directed circular order, not every original linear adjacency: it joins the two original endpoints and introduces a content-defined cut. It can also change compression-block membership and Dice populations. These are explicit limitations, not pure measured recency removal.
predictions: After native checks, supplied_bridge should reproduce incumbent probabilities, gradients, one-step updates, buffers and full metrics; lexical_bridge should match g1-r0060-lexical_workmatched. Failure blocks interpretation.

canonical_ring should exceed lexical_bridge by an exploratory practically interesting AUC margin0.0005 if relative circular order is useful under this representation. Report raw differences regardless of this heuristic; it is not a significance test.

If direction is dispensable, canonical_dihedral should retain most ring quality. A ring advantage over dihedral instead motivates a direction diagnostic; the earlier reversal result is not conclusive.

If both canonical rings approach lexical/hash quality while supplied remains stronger, supplied boundary or its interaction with compression is a better next hypothesis; this outcome alone does not prove recency or refute other order models.

Canonical ring is invariant to cyclic shifts, dihedral is invariant to cyclic shifts and reversal, lexical to arbitrary valid-event permutations. Ring is intentionally not invariant to arbitrary permutations. No fitted or cost result is predicted as established.
falsifiers: Native source parity, finite-loss/backward, mask conservation or claimed symmetry failures invalidate any mechanistic AUC reading.
Ring/dihedral no better than lexical after corresponding training falsifies useful circular-order retention for the tested candidate and recipe, not all possible order dependence.
Equal or better canonical performance than supplied weakens useful endpoint dependence; confirm with registered paired repetitions before asserting stability.
An advantage explained by initialization, compression/normalization behavior, additional computation or one-seed variation is insufficient for an information mechanism claim.
alternative_explanations: The original linear endpoints may encode useful supplied-position associations; no raw timestamps establish their temporal meaning.
Circular wraparound introduces one artificial neighbor pair and removes one original linear pair; content anchor and block membership alter compression and batch-normalization optimization.
Long/periodic/duplicate histories can have special symmetry stabilizers; complete tuples and exact ranking avoid source-position tie leakage, but do not eliminate representational differences.
Single-seed optimization and adaptive reuse of validation can exaggerate differences; all comparisons are exploratory.
All auxiliary task AUCs can regress while click improves, as inherited joint model versus DIN already demonstrates; auxiliary mean is never selection score.
Matched parameters, branches and passes do not establish equal wall/GPU cost.
